sentences.text: Some water always gets in, so you need a reliable way to get it out.
Automatic electric pumps with float switches handle the everyday leaks and the rain.
A high-water alarm, loud enough to hear at the helm, tells you when something is wrong.
Without one, how do you find out your bilge is filling?
When the boat starts handling badly.
Carry a manual pump too, for the day the electrics fail.
Don’t trust the number on the pump’s label.
Its capacity drops sharply with the height it has to lift the water, and with the length of the hose.
And most important of all: know where every through-hull on your boat is.
You can’t close a seacock you can’t find.
